For the third time in five such games, lefty-swinging Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon was out of the lineup against a right-handed starter to open Tuesday’s doubleheader.
In all three instances, righty-swinging José Caballero started at third base instead.
Manager Aaron Boone chalked Tuesday afternoon’s decision up to Tampa Bay Rays starter Nick Martinez having reverse splits — meaning he’s actually tougher against lefties — and said McMahon would start the nightcap against a more traditional righty in Drew Rasmussen.
That would also allow the sure-handed McMahon to play defense on a night Max Fried, who regularly elicits grounders to third base, was starting for the Yankees.
But as McMahon continues to struggle, this is a trend to watch with the MLB postseason rapidly approaching.
“I want to be playing them both and getting them both regular reps,” Boone said before Tuesday’s first game, “so [it was] more just picking what game I wanted to play Caballero.”
Entering Tuesday, McMahon was hitting just .150 with a .402 OPS and no home runs since Sept. 1, when he returned from the injured list for a left thumb sprain.
Overall, he is batting .208 with 10 homers and a .618 OPS.
While his season-long numbers against right-handed pitchers (.639 OPS) are superior to his stats against lefties (.518 OPS), McMahon’s offensive production has been modest either way.
Caballero was already the preferred third-base option against left-handed starters, but now he’s seeing more playing time there against right-handers, too.
A utilityman by trade, Caballero began Tuesday with a .237 average, 10 home runs and a .676 OPS against right-handed pitching.
Caballero’s previous two starts against right-handers came on Sunday against Arizona’s Corbin Burnes, whose splits are fairly even for his career, and last week against Minnesota’s Bailey Ober, who is better against righties than lefties.
That means Caballero isn’t only getting chances against right-handed pitchers with reverse splits.
And while McMahon’s calling card is typically his glove, the advanced metrics have not been favorable to the 31-year-old this season.
McMahon entered Tuesday with -1 Defensive Runs Saved and 1 Outs Above Average — down considerably from his 10 DRS and 7 OAA in 2025.
His numbers at third base this year are comparable to those of Caballero, who began the day with 0 DRS and -1 OAA.
Caballero is also much more dynamic on the bases, as he began the doubleheader with 32 stolen bases. However, starting Caballero eliminates the ability to use him as a pinch-runner — an element of his game that makes him a valuable late-inning weapon come October.
Third base isn’t the Yankees’ only infield position with some uncertainty.
Since being replaced at shortstop by George Lombard Jr. and recalled from Triple-A, Anthony Volpe has performed admirably as the Yankees’ second baseman.
The righty-hitting Volpe began Tuesday hitting .286 with a .753 OPS since being recalled on Sept. 10. He had been worth 1 DRS and 1 OAA at second base over that small sample, too.
Volpe is not going to supplant second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was set to be activated for the second game of the doubleheader after a short IL stint for a right thumb sprain.
But Volpe could challenge for playing time at second base against left-handed pitching, against whom he is hitting .240 with a .680 OPS in the majors this season.
The lefty-swinging Chisholm has endured a down season against lefties, batting .221 with a .654 OPS and a team-worst 35% strikeout rate in those matchups.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” Boone said, “but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
The 28-year-old Chisholm wasn’t thrilled last year when the Yankees sat him against left-handed Boston Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet in Game 1 of their Wild Card series.
But with the Yankees likely to face the lefty-heavy Red Sox in the Wild Card round again next week, Boone and company will have more decisions to make at second and third — especially because offense would be at a premium if Aaron Judge (calf) can’t return in time.

BRONX, NY — Jazz Chisholm Jr. is set to be activated from the 10-day injured list following the first game of the Yankees’ doubleheader on Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
The second baseman missed two weeks after spraining his thumb, and his spot was filled in admirably by Anthony Volpe — the cast-off shortstop who has enjoyed a minor renaissance, of sorts. Entering Tuesday’s action, he had hit safely in six of his 10 games since being called back up from Triple-A, adding a home run and seven RBI. Five of them came in his first game back on Sept. 10 against the Colorado Rockies.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that Chisholm is “in a good spot” after hitting and throwing over the past several days. How playing time will shake out remains to be seen.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job, but looking forward to getting Jazz back as well.”
With the opportunity for playing time seemingly available at third base with Jose Caballero, Ryan McMahon, and Amed Rosario in the mix, Boone had said that “we’ll see” when asked about Volpe potentially moving to the hot corner. Volpe said he has yet to have those conversations with team brass.
It has been a down season for Chisholm, who owns a .715 OPS with 19 home runs and 55 RBI. After a 30/30 season last year, he came into the 2026 campaign hoping to make a run at 50/50.
That did not happen, but getting a healthy Chisholm back who could possibly recapture last year’s spark would provide a significant boost for the Yankees, who are facing the very real possibility of being without Aaron Judge for their Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox next week.

This four-game tilt against the Rays in the penultimate series of the season had the chance to be a blockbuster showdown to decide the division. However, the Yankees losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks removed a lot of the jeopardy from this series, New York now needing to sweep just to avoid being eliminated from the AL East title race and depending on a very unlikely collapse from Tampa in their final series of the season to keep the divisional door the slightest bit ajar. All the same, this could be a preview of a prospective ALCS showdown, so I expect both teams to come out firing. The first game of today’s doubleheader is a makeup of the rainout from May 23rd.
Carlos Rodón finds himself in the unexpected position of being on the postseason rotation bubble. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are seemingly locks which would pit Rodón against Gerrit Cole for that final spot if they roll out a three-man rotation. It almost comes down to a style choice at that point — Rodón walks almost three times as many batters as Cole, but surrenders about half as many home runs per nine. He’s a good choice to start a game against the Rays — in six starts against Tampa with the Yankees, Rodón has a 3.69 ERA and 31.3-percent strikeout rate in 31.2 innings. In 15 starts this season, Rodón is 6-3 with a 2.95 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.69 FIP, and 83 strikeouts in 76.1 innings.
The Rays have a maddening habit of transforming other teams’ castoffs into rotation stars. This season’s example is longtime journeyman Nick Martinez, who had pitched as a swingman the previous four years in San Diego and Cincinnati. Martinez owns the lowest walk rate (3.5-percent) of any qualified starter, using deception and precise command to induce soft contact. He’s technically got a six-pitch mix but usually sticks with sinker, changeup, cutter, and four-seamer. In 29 starts, Martinez is 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.98 FIP, and 101 strikeouts in 171.1 innings.
This is more or less the Yankees’ go-to lineup for the rest of the regular season with Aaron Judge on the IL. Heliot Ramos and Spencer Jones are both going to get a lot of run out in the outfield, so it was encouraging to see them both hit home runs against the former Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes in their last game. The Rays have their three-headed slugging monster atop lineup and then stack the bottom two-thirds with speed. Junior Caminero is third in MLB with 41 home runs giving him back-to-back 40-HR seasons. Chandler Simpson is MLB’s stolen base leader with 46 and third in batting average at .309, but is the only qualified hitter in baseball without a home run this season.

item.content:encoded:
It was easy for everybody to get ahead of themselves when Anthony Volpe had a big first game back against the Colorado Rockies. Jazz Chisholm Jr. had just gone down, and Volpe delivered a three-hit night capped by a grand slam. At that point, Volpe had gone through a torrid home run streak in the minors, so the thought was that if he replicated it in the big leagues, maybe he could usurp Chisholm.
While Volpe's teammates at Triple-A saw the version of him that closely resembled an infield Barry Bonds, he just wasn't that after that first game. Since then, Volpe has gone 7-for-33. He didn't hit a home run and had just two doubles in that span. In many ways, his .226/.263/.290 slash line is about where he has always been as a big leaguer.
That is why, since Chisholm will be playing in the second game of Tuesday night's doubleheader vs. the Rays, per Chris Kirschner of The Athletic, there's no reason to debate who takes second base. The answer is easily Chisholm. Chisholm hasn't had the best season, but in the postseason, he's more of a threat at the plate and on the basepaths. Chisholm has 19 homers this year with 40 stolen bases. Overall, he's hitting .232/.312/.403 at the plate.
Then, of course, there's the defense. That's why a hitter who's been at or below a 100 wRC+ all year can post a 3.2 WAR, according to FanGraphs. This year, Chisholm also has 12 Outs Above Average at the position, per Baseball Savant.
It does feel like Chisholm is the priority, too, once he's back. According to manager Aaron Boone, when asked about Volpe's status and the possibility of him playing at third base, the focus was on getting Chisholm back.
"We'll see," Boone said of Volpe getting reps at the hot corner, according to the New York Post's Greg Joyce. "First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we'll figure it out as the week unfolds, how I want to play it."
Potential infield configuration against a lefty
If the Yankees face a tough lefty in October and aren't too keen on playing Ryan McMahon, who has a 74 wRC+, and Chisholm, they might have a choice here. They could stick with Chisholm at second and have either Jose Caballero or Anthony Volpe play third base.
They could also have Chisholm go back to third base and have Volpe at second. That way, they keep the better player on the field while also getting a righty at second or third.
With Aaron Judge out, Chisholm could boost the lineup. He's had a tough year, but a big October could make up for some regular-season woes.

After Chisholm got hurt diving into second base Sept. 8, the Yankees called up Anthony Volpe to get some run at the position he had mostly transitioned to at Triple-A, and he made the most of it.
In the 10 games since Volpe was recalled, he has started at second base nine times (José Caballero started the other) and mostly looked sharp, batting .286 with a .753 OPS and four steals.
Whether Volpe has done enough to warrant at-bats once Chisholm returns remains to be seen. Shortly before he was called back up, the natural shortstop had also started to mix in some third base, starting three games there, though Aaron Boone would only offer, “We’ll see,” when asked whether that could be an option for Volpe with Chisholm back.
“First things first, getting Jazz back and then we’ll figure it out as the week unfolds how I want to play it,” Boone said.
The Yankees have not gotten much offensive production from their third basemen this year, especially of late. Since returning from his own thumb sprain Sept. 1, Ryan McMahon has hit just 6-for-40 (.150) with a .402 OPS, with Caballero starting at third over him Sunday against a righty. Amed Rosario has often started at third against lefties, and while he has not hit in line with his career numbers, the Yankees continue to believe he will.
Boone could also platoon Volpe and Chisholm at second base, as the lefty-hitting Chisholm is batting only .221 with a .654 OPS against lefties. But the pending free agent had just been starting to get hot in a disappointing season, hitting .391 with a 1.028 OPS over his last 15 games before getting hurt.
If and where Volpe fits on the playoff roster is just one of the many decisions they will have to consider over this final week of the regular season.
“You know it’s going to take a lot of players and a lot of people when you get to spring training and the season unfolds,” Boone said. “We’ll have hopefully some tough decisions to make when we’re setting postseason rosters and things like that. But that’s a better problem to have.”

Clarke Schmidt was expected to see the team doctor early this week after experiencing biceps cramping while warming up Sunday, which kept him from entering the game. The right-hander had just made his return from Tommy John surgery and is trying to carve out a role in the playoff bullpen.
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) could also have a role in a playoff bullpen, but first the lefty will need to face hitters this week as he tries to show the Yankees he could jump right into postseason action without pitching in a game since he got hurt Aug. 22.

With Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially coming off the injured list on Tuesday, former Yankees manager Joe Girardi is suggesting a position change heading into the postseason.
Anthony Volpe now seems entrenched at second base, but Girardi, the last man to lead the Yankees to a World Series in 2009, thinks there's another position for which Chisholm, who has been out with a right thumb sprain, would be suited.
Asked by reporters if he would move Volpe over to third base with the playoffs approaching, manager Aaron Boone said, "We'll see."
"I would think that you would possibly move Jazz over there [to third base] because Jazz has done it," Girardi said on the YES Network during the Yankees' 8-4 loss Sunday to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
"He swung the bat pretty well over there, too," Girardi added. "It didn't seem to phase the offensive part of his game."
Last season, Chisholm played 29 games at third base with a fielding percentage of .920. This season, he has yet to play a game at third.
A year ago, Chisholm batted .242 with 31 home runs, 80 RBIs, 31 stolen bases and an .813 OPS.

This year, Chisholm is batting .232 with 19 homers and 55 RBI and a .715 OPS.
Third baseman Ryan McMahon, a left-handed hitter, has been struggling offensively. The Yankees started right-handed hitting Jose Caballero on Sunday against right-handed starter Corbin Burnes.
"Caballero's had a good [road] trip, had a good night last night," Girardi said. "He can get really hot...and can do a lot of different things. I think you gotta play him."

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

We know what you’re thinking: The New York Yankees cannot realistically replace Aaron Judge.
Unfortunately for Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman, they have no choice. Judge landed back on the injured list with a right calf strain, and the earliest that he could return is next Sunday’s regular-season finale against the Orioles. The Yankees have not committed to the three-time AL MVP potentially being ready for the AL Wild Card Series.
“I usually deal with calf stuff all year long,” Judge told reporters on Saturday. “It usually doesn’t get to [the media], and I usually don’t miss any games. So that was kind of the same thing I was feeling. I was working my way back, and then something kind of grabs you at a strange time.”
So, who will man right field in Judge’s absence? Will it be Spencer Jones, who has flashed as a rookie? What about Cody Bellinger, who could shift over from left field?
As it turns out, the answer might be speedy utilityman José Caballero. Seriously.
José Caballero could start in the Yankees’ outfield following Aaron Judge’s latest injury
The 30-year-old Caballero drew the start in center field on Saturday night, hitting two singles and drawing the walk in a 5-3 loss. He's played 20 of his 130 games in the outfield, with most of that action coming in the corner spots.
For what it’s worth, we’ve always liked Caballero enough that we repeatedly advocated for the Yankees to consider naming him the full-time shortstop and trading Anthony Volpe. So we’re not opposed to the thought of him playing right, with Bellinger starting in center and Heliot Ramos taking over in left field.
The 5-foot-9, 190-pound Caballero's calling card has always been his legs, and he's stolen at least 26 bases in each of his first four seasons. This year has been no exception, with him swiping a team-leading 32 bases in 43 attempts. But to his credit, Caballero has added some power to his game, recording a career-high 14 home runs in nearly 450 plate appearances.
Bellinger has played 118 of his 127 games in left field, though he has extensive experience in both center and right. The reigning All-Star Game MVP is also one of the Yankees' most reliable hitters, even as his OPS has dropped from .813 to .781.
Objectively speaking, the Yankees can afford to have an outfield consisting of Caballero, Bellinger, and either Ramos or Jones. Trent Grisham remains out with a right hamstring problem, though Boone has hinted they’d get the two-time Gold Glove winner back in time for the playoffs. As things stand, the Yankees would host the rival Red Sox in a first-round rematch of last year’s Wild Card Series.
Ideally for the Yankees, they’ll have Judge batting second and playing right field next Tuesday night. But if you’re looking for a dark horse candidate to shine this postseason, you could do far worse than the versatile Caballero.

The New York Yankees are looking to end a 17-year World Series drought.
Aaron Boone has completed eight of those years as Yankees manager.
This could be a crucial postseason for Boone's future with the AL East club, but New York's ownership and front office have always shown confidence in the skipper.
If three-time MVP Aaron Judge is unable to play in the postseason due to his calf strain, the Yankees will face a difficult task to end their World Series-less streak.
Elsewhere on the diamond, Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes Boone will have to hit the right buttons with the infield alignment.
"However, Aaron Boone is about to be in second-guessing hell in October as it pertains to when and where to deploy George Lombard Jr., Anthony Volpe, José Caballero, Amed Rosario and Ryan McMahon at shortstop and third base," Miller wrote.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. would complicate things further if he returns from the injured list before the playoffs.
Volpe has been playing well at second base, but Chisholm offers a higher offensive ceiling.
Boone could consider moving Volpe or Chisholm to third base to keep both players in the lineup. If so, does Caballero become limited to pinch-running duties?
McMahon is Boone's best defensive third baseman, but he offers little (.208/.275/.343, .618 OPS) with a bat in hand.
It seems likely Lombard will stick at shortstop, but Boone and his coaching staff have to be racking his brain trying to figure out what's best for the team.

item.content:encoded:
Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality.
“Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East.
Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium this week, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday.
Aaron Boone acknowledged that his team will probably have to sweep the Rays just for a crack at the division crown, as FanGraphs gave the Yankees a measly 2.7% chance of winning the AL East before Sunday’s game.
“There’s still a chance,” Cam Schlittler said, “but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
While the Yankees still technically have a shot to defy the odds, the far likelier scenario is that their postseason begins on Sept. 29 at home against Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year.
With that in mind, let’s try to predict what the club’s roster could look like for that series.
Hitters (15): Ben Rice, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones, Trent Grisham, Cody Bellinger, Ryan McMahon, George Lombard Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Luis García Jr., Jazz Chisholm Jr., José Caballero, Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez, Anthony Volpe, Amed Rosario
With the Yankees providing minimal info on Aaron Judge’s calf strain, it can’t be assumed he’ll be available.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return from a sprained thumb as soon as Tuesday. Meanwhile, Trent Grisham is still in play as a playoff option as he recovers from a hamstring strain, but Boone said that activating him before the end of the regular season is “complicated,” partly due to roster logistics.
With Max Schuemann presumably the corresponding move for Chisholm, the Yankees would have to option someone else if they activated Grisham before the playoffs. That someone wouldn’t be able to be recalled for 10 days barring a new injury; it seems like Jasson Domínguez is being protected from that window in case he’s needed for the Wild Card roster.
Grisham has been doing baseball activities and is “pretty deep into his running progression,” Boone said. If he is on the Wild Card roster, the Yankees will have an interesting decision to make between him and Spencer Jones in center field.
Third base could also be a conundrum, as Ryan McMahon and José Caballero don’t offer much offensively, and Amed Rosario is a poor defender. He’s only on the roster as an option against lefties, even though he hasn’t been great against them.
Another idea would be to use Volpe, who has been playing second, at third against lefties since he played a few games there in the minors this season. However, he doesn’t have a strong arm, and he hasn’t been working at third base since being recalled. Volpe said that the Yankees have not talked to him about manning the hot corner before the regular season ends.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we’ll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it.”
Volpe can also play second over Chisholm against lefties.
Pitchers (11): Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Clarke Schmidt, John Schreiber, Tim Hill, Ryan Weathers
As things stand, Carlos Rodón, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are scheduled to pitch against the Rays, in that order. That would give Cole, who has struggled to get swing-and-miss, an extra day of rest if he were to start Game 1 of the Wild Card round. Schlittler, the AL Cy Young frontrunner, would be on regular rest if tabbed for Game 1.
Because the Wild Card round is a best-of-three series, Rodón isn’t needed, especially with Will Warren expected to work out of the bullpen and able to provide length.
Warren, slated to make one more start this season after struggling on Sunday, is one of a few converted starters who could impact the Bombers’ bullpen this postseason. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are the others. Schmidt, being cautious in his return from Tommy John surgery, couldn’t come into Sunday’s game due to some bicep cramping, while Weathers isn’t expected to return from a flexor strain before the regular season ends.
Still, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled out the idea of Weathers’ first game back coming in the playoffs.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”
As for the relievers that the Yankees have leaned on all season, David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick headline the group. All have been used heavily, especially Headrick.
The lefty allowed a grand slam to Nolan Arenado and saw his fastball velocity down an average of 1.3 mph during his major league-leading 79th appearance on Sunday, but he insisted that he feels fine physically. Boone also downplayed concerns over Headrick’s ongoing velocity fluctuations, though he did say that he hopes to get him and other relievers “in a good spot” with some rest ahead of the playoffs.
That said, the Yankees still haven’t been eliminated from the AL East race. They’ll keep trying to take the division from the Rays until they are.
“We’re going to show up Tuesday,” Boone said, “and try and kick their butt.”

On Sunday, the New York Yankees lost the final game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 8-4 (at Chase Field).
The Yankees also dropped two out of three games in the series.
Jose Caballero finished with one strikeout and no hits in four at-bats.
Bryan Hoch of MLB.com wrote: “Ballgame over, Arizona wins. 8-4 is your final at Chase Field. The Yankees dropped two of three in the desert. They’re 6 games behind Tampa Bay with 7 to play.”
Jose Caballero Makes Bold Statement
After the game, Caballero met with the media (via YES Network).
Reporter: “Barrage of home runs for you guys there in that third inning to knock Burns out. But aside from that the offense was very quiet. What were they doing, their relievers in particular, that really held you guys down?”
Caballero: “Like you said, I think we put good swings early in the game. And whenever the bullpen came in, they were dotting pitches. They were doing their thing. And like I said, I feel like we need to play better. We need to try to cut some of the bad innings and try to do something different. But I think we’re going to be just fine in the postseason.”
Reporter: “What tells you that?”
Caballero: “This team, what we’ve been doing the whole year. And I’ve seen it before. So it’s no concern about the team offensively or pitching-wise. So just waiting for the postseason and do our best in the postseason. That was our first goal. And from now it’s a race to the title.”
Caballero is in the middle of his fourth season in the MLB (and second with the Yankees).
He has also spent time with the Tampa Bay Rays and Seattle Mariners.
Looking At The Yankees Right Now
The Yankees will now return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday afternoon in the Bronx.
They are the second-place team in the American League East with an 89-66 record in 155 games.
Currently, the Yankees are 6.0 games back of the Rays.

The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we'll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who's finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he'll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn't totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He's always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn't have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We've seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who'll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night's hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.

Los panameños Iván Herrera y José Caballero tuvieron una jornada destacada en las Grandes Ligas, con buenas producciones al bate, aunque sus equipos, Cardenales de San Luis y Yankees de Nueva York, terminaron perdiendo sus respectivos partidos el sábado 19 de septiembre.
Iván Herrera, de 5-3 con doblete en la derrota de San Luis
Herrera fue uno de los más activos en la ofensiva de los Cardenales: se fue de 5-3 con un doblete y un ponche. A pesar de su aporte, San Luis cayó 8-5 ante los Nacionales de Washington en el Busch Stadium. José Caballero, perfecto al plato en la caída de los Yankees
José Caballero, conocido como “Chema” o “Cabby”, tuvo una noche perfecta al plato: se fue de 2-2 y además recibió un pasaporte en la derrota de los Yankees 5-3 frente a los Diamondbacks de Arizona en el Chase Field. Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado. Jake McCarthy and TJ Rumfield each produced an RBI.
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle, which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Padres 6, Marlins 5 (10 innings)
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning and San Diego edged visiting Miami.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and Los Angeles stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a victory over visiting San Francisco.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
Angels 6, Twins 5 (11 innings)Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as Los Angeles edged Minnesota in Anaheim, Calif.Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home. Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels, who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on Vaughn Grissom's homer.Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for the Twins.

PHOENIX — Los Yankees llegaron a Arizona con el objetivo de mantener su puesto en la postemporada, sin dejar de luchar por una oportunidad cada vez más lejana de ganar la División Este de la Liga Americana. Para el sábado por la noche, la clasificación ya no era más que una parte del problema.
El propio Chase Field se había convertido en algo con lo que Aaron Boone tenía que lidiar.
Nueva York llegaba al domingo con un balance de 89-65 tras perder por 5-3 en la última entrada ante los Diamondbacks, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay cuando solo quedan ocho partidos por disputar. Los Yankees seguían ocupando el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana, pero su margen para hacer frente a otra lesión se había reducido después de que Aaron Judge volviera a la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha.
Las decisiones de Boone del sábado reflejaron esa realidad. José Caballero fue titular en el centro del campo por segunda vez esta temporada. Cody Bellinger se quedó en la izquierda en lugar de cambiar de posición, a pesar de que tiene mucha experiencia jugando en el centro del campo. Boone explicó más tarde que Bellinger también estaba notando el estrés acumulado por la superficie sintética y que no quería aumentar la carga sobre él.
Esa cautela se mantuvo durante todo el partido, que los Yankees acabaron perdiendo por un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada. También fue importante porque Nueva York está a punto de marcharse de Arizona para afrontar una serie crucial de cuatro partidos contra Tampa Bay en el Yankee Stadium, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada en la que se repartirán las victorias. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el equipo sigue buscando el equilibrio entre la lucha por el título de división y mantener intacta su plantilla para octubre.
La preocupación por el estado del césped dejó de ser un simple detalle de gestión de la alineación en cuanto Boone explicó por qué faltaba otro titular. Los Yankees habían llegado a un punto en el que un pie lesionado más podía complicar tanto su alineación en los jardines como la profundidad de plantilla que podrían necesitar durante la última semana.
Ese cálculo es especialmente importante en el centro del campo, donde Boone tiene menos combinaciones con las que está acostumbrado a trabajar una vez que empieza a proteger a los jugadores de las lesiones. Un ajuste de una sola noche puede convertirse rápidamente en un problema para la plantilla si las molestias persisten de cara a la recta final de la temporada.
Jones se queda fuera tras un repunte del dolor en el talón al jugar sobre césped artificial
Spencer Jones no jugó el sábado por unas molestias en el pie izquierdo y el talón, después de haberse dado un golpe en el talón a principios de semana en Minnesota. Jones dijo que las molestias se agravaron por el desgaste de haber jugado el viernes por la noche en el césped del Chase Field.
El novato restó importancia al tema antes del partido y dijo que esperaba que la baja durara solo un día.
«No es nada grave», dijo Jones.
Jones describió el problema como una molestia más que como una nueva lesión aguda. También lo relacionó directamente con la superficie y con los impactos que habían absorbido sus pies.
«Solo estoy un poco magullado», dijo Jones. «Jugar sobre césped artificial es diferente, es duro para los pies».
Boone dijo que la situación de Jones se evaluaría día a día y que estuvo a punto de dejarlo en la alineación. También dejó claro que los Yankees no consideraban que Jones estuviera fuera de combate.
«Simplemente me pareció que, sobre todo al estar aquí en el césped artificial, se había dado un golpe en el talón en Minnesota y, al volver a jugar en césped [el viernes], creo que es algo que hay que valorar día a día», dijo Boone. «Incluso creo que podría jugar esta noche».
Las declaraciones de Boone tras el partido son lo que más tranquilidad dan
Jones no llegó a salir en el partido del sábado, pero Boone dijo después que la decisión se debió más a la situación del partido que a motivos médicos. El entrenador dijo que habría sacado a Jones si los Yankees hubieran tenido el enfrentamiento adecuado o lo hubieran necesitado al final del partido.
«Estaba disponible, igual que yo lo habría estado… si hubiera surgido una oportunidad de batear o hubiéramos tenido que hacer algo, habría recurrido a él», dijo Boone.
Esa distinción es importante. A Jones no le han dado de baja, ni lo han puesto en la lista de lesionados, ni le han prohibido hacer nada relacionado con el béisbol. El domingo por la mañana, los Yankees seguían considerando el problema como una molestia pasajera.
La profundidad en el centro del campo hace que un día de descanso cobre más importancia
Los Yankees pueden permitirse que se pierda un solo partido. La situación de la plantilla se complica si Jones necesita más tiempo.
Jones ha jugado 80 partidos esta temporada y tiene un promedio de bateo de .248, con un porcentaje de embasado de .318 y un porcentaje de slugging de .433. Lleva 10 jonrones, 12 dobles, un triple, 38 carreras impulsadas y nueve bases robadas en 265 turnos al bate. Baseball Savant le atribuye 23 hits de más de una base, es decir, uno cada 11,5 turnos al bate.
Su valía también se nota en cómo los Yankees pueden colocar al resto del equipo. Caballero puede jugar de central, pero el sábado fue solo su segunda titularidad en esa posición esta temporada. Boone decidió expresamente no cambiar a Bellinger al centro por culpa del césped artificial y de la propia carga de trabajo de Bellinger.
Los Yankees también llamaron a Max Schuemann cuando Judge entró en la lista de lesionados, dando prioridad a la versatilidad defensiva. Esa decisión le da a Boone otra opción en todas las posiciones del campo y en los jardines, pero no sustituye la potencia de Jones como bateador zurdo ni su papel habitual en el centro del campo.
Los Yankees llegan a la última jornada de la serie con una duda sobre su estado físico
Los Yankees cierran la serie contra Arizona el domingo, antes del día de descanso del lunes. Ese descanso le da a Jones un poco más de tiempo para recuperarse antes de los cuatro partidos contra los Rays en tres días en el Yankee Stadium.
Por ahora, el último informe médico sigue siendo alentador. Jones espera que las molestias sean pasajeras, Boone lo consideraba apto para jugar el sábado y el club no ha dado a entender que se esté planteando incluirlo en la lista de lesionados.
La pregunta que queda es si un día de descanso del césped del Chase Field será suficiente para que el talón se recupere antes de que los Yankees empiecen la serie más importante que les queda en el calendario de la temporada regular.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be.
A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be.
A scenario is now potentially unfolding that would have only appeared in Boone's nightmares: a postseason without the best hitter in baseball, with a lineup that struggled mightily without him. Even if they seemed to gradually improve as time went on, particularly in August, it would be a massive blow if he cannot return.
You can't replace a guy like Judge midseason; you can merely do your best to make up for his absence. Fortunately, on a platoon-heavy team like this, they should have plenty of options to build a lineup without him for the playoffs.
What the playoff lineup should look like against right-handed pitching
- Ben Rice (DH)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Luis García Jr. (1B)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Austin Wells (C)
- Ryan McMahon (3B)
This lineup simultaneously features the easiest decisions, but also the roughest circumstances. Having a guy like Judge as the ultimate lineup balancer who mashed both lefties and righties allowed you to use plenty of left-handed hitters at the top of the order, something that the team has in abundance.
The best right-handed hitter on the roster without Judge is hard to pinpoint, especially since all of them are significantly worse against same-handed pitching. Heliot Ramos might just be the best option to bat highest among them, which would be cleanup in this scenario.
It's not an ideal situation in the slightest. Even if you don't think it makes sense to bat Ramos that high because of his struggles against righties, there is some merit to breaking up the team's many left-handed bats. In a lineup that will likely only feature one other righty, it has to be considered.
The fate of this lineup when they're out there, which would likely be mostly after a potential Wild Card Series with the Red Sox, would hinge on the middle. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. got hot in August and helped the offensive turnaround begin, but both are heavily streaky bats with contact issues. If they go cold, this lineup might limp through games like they did in July.
What the playoff lineup should look like against left-handed pitching
- Paul Goldschmidt (1B)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Ben Rice (DH)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- Anthony Volpe/José Caballero (3B)
- Austin Wells (C)
Here's where it gets interesting. How far do you lean into the platoons on a team with several players designated to specifically hit lefties, especially against a team that will likely lean heavily on those types of pitchers in Boston?
Many Yankees fans believe that it would be improper to take a guy like García, who is likely the team's second-best pound-for-pound hitter with Judge injured, out of the lineup, but you don't really have a choice here. He's slashing just .238/.274/.363 against lefties, while Goldschmidt has been among the team's best hitters against them for the last two seasons. Add in Rice's improvements against same-handed pitching, and it just needs to be done.
Using him in a different position is also just not happening. He has not played second base, where he was extremely poor, since 2025. The only position he's played this season is first base. If he wasn't so dreadful out there, maybe he could replace Chisholm, a mediocre hitter against lefties in his own right.
Speaking of defense, you might notice the lack of Amed Rosario, and that's intentional. Rosario's use on this roster was almost exclusively predicated on his ability to hit left-handed pitching, but he's been significantly worse at it this season. Add in his truly dreadful defense, and you have a conundrum.
Anthony Volpe is a better hitter than José Caballero, but there are questions about how his arm strength would play at third, where he's also very inexperienced with just three games played in Triple-A. Caballero would probably get the nod here, but he's someone who just plays better off the bench with his speed and versatility.
It's also an aggressive placement for Lombard, batting fifth in his first career playoff game. The results haven't quite been there yet for him, but he's always been significantly better against lefties and should be slid up the lineup and be treated as one of those platoon bats who are there to hit that handedness, even if it might lead to consequences in the bullpen.
Boston is loaded with left-handed pitching from the rotation to the bullpen, so there will be few opportunities to get to a guy like García on the bench. The rest of the bench would be situational with pinch runners and pinch hitters.
Things ultimately look particularly shallow, but is there a chance that some last-minute reinforcements could help out?
Could Trent Grisham or Giancarlo Stanton return to provide relief?
It seems unlikely, especially early in the postseason, but the Yankees are refusing to shut the door on either Trent Grisham's or Giancarlo Stanton's return.
Grisham, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain earlier this month, was revealed to be "pretty far along" in his running program, and Boone said it's not out of the question that he returns in the season's final days, although an exact timeline for that has not been spelled out. If Grisham is physically ready to get back on the field, it would provide a boost, even if he might not be starting over Jones at this point.
Stanton, who's been out since April due to two separate calf strains and a re-aggravation, has continued to hit through his rehab, but hasn't resumed running as of last Sunday. Considering how it took several weeks for him to even get close to back from injury with his running program last time, this likely doesn't put him in play until the ALCS at the earliest.
While Stanton seems significantly less likely to get into a game again this season, there is a path for Grisham. The team could use him and Ramos in a platoon situation to add yet another lefty to the lineup against right-handed pitching. They could also utilize him as a pinch hitter on a larger bench than usual, due to the team's propensity to carry fewer than 13 pitchers in the Wild Card Series.
The real question for Grisham is defensive. While Jones has absolutely looked shaky in center field, the struggles of Grisham out there are well documented. Add in his diminished athleticism and likely balky hamstring straight off an injury, would it be better if the team just chanced it by throwing him in right field when he plays?
He hasn't played the position since a disastrous error lost the Brewers the 2019 Wild Card Game against the Nationals, but playing it at Yankee Stadium is significantly easier than dealing with the spacious center field. Of course, this is something the Yankees would have to determine their willingness to do beforehand and have him practice the position, so what plans they have will be determined by that.
As for Stanton if he's ever medically able to get back? There just might not be any room for him with Rice as the permanent DH. You don't want to take the bat out of either of their hands, and with the team seemingly having to juggle multiple guys coming off soft-tissue injuries, can they afford to use a roster spot for a designated pinch hitter as they did with 2022 Matt Carpenter?

item.content:encoded:
Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 389-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
The D-backs (81-74) gained a game on Philadelphia (85-70) for the third spot in the National League wild-card race but are still four games back with seven games to play.
Yankees starter and American League Cy Young candidate Cam Schlittler gave up three hits and three runs (one earned) in six innings, leaving when his pitch count reached 98. His season high is 106.
Schlittler struck out three and walked six while lowering his ERA to an American League-leading 1.94. He has given up one earned run or fewer in each of his last eight starts.
Arizona starter Brandon Pfaadt gave up four singles and one run in 4 1/3 innings, leaving after the Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth. Ben Rice hit a sacrifice fly off Justin Martinez to break a scoreless tie. Pfaadt struck out three and walked one.
The D-backs broke up Schlittler's no-hitter with a two-run fifth. Both runs scored after Schlittler's one-out fielding error.
Arenado had Arizona's first hit, a line single to left field with one out, before Tim Tawa pushed a bunt toward the mound. Schlittler could not field the ball cleanly and both runners were safe.
Lawlar lined a two-out triple to left-center on a 99 mph fastball for a 2-1 lead.
Ramos and Wells homered in the sixth to put the Yankees in front 3-2.
The D-backs tied it in the sixth when Ketel Marte and Gabriel Moreno drew four-pitch walks and Geraldo Perdomo beat out a two-strike bunt single to load the bases. Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly before Schlittler struck out Arenado and Tawa with runners on second and third.
--Field Level Media

The New York Yankees suffered a tough loss on Saturday night, falling to the Arizona Diamondbacks 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s two-run walk-off home run in the ninth inning.
The loss came after the Yankees twice held a lead earlier in the game. New York broke through in the fifth inning when Austin Wells, Anthony Volpe and José Caballero opened the frame with consecutive singles to load the bases. Ben Rice followed with a sacrifice fly that brought home Wells and put the Yankees ahead 1-0.
Arizona answered in the bottom half of the inning, taking a 2-1 lead on Jordan Lawler’s two-run triple. Both runs were unearned against Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, who committed a fielding error on a sacrifice bunt during the inning.
New York responded quickly in the sixth. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a solo home run before Wells put the Yankees back in front with his 13th home run of the season. Both home runs came against Arizona reliever Kevin Ginkel.
Schlittler ran into trouble again in the bottom of the sixth after issuing two walks and allowing a single to load the bases with nobody out. Corbin Carroll tied the game with a sacrifice fly, but Schlittler struck out the next two batters to escape further damage.
Schlittler completed six innings, allowing three runs on three hits with three walks and six strikeouts over 98 pitches. Only one of the three runs was earned, and his season earned-run average dropped to 1.94.
Neither team scored again until the ninth, when Smith ended the game with his two-run homer off Michael Fulmer.
The Yankees will finish the series Sunday at 4:10 p.m. Will Warren will face Corbin Burnes.

But after the Yankees just lost Aaron Judge to the injured list again with a right calf strain, the last thing they needed was Jones nursing an injury of his own.
“Just a little banged up,” Jones said before Saturday’s game against the Diamondbacks. “Playing on turf is different, hard on the feet.”
Aaron Boone also downplayed it, adding that he still almost kept Jones in the lineup before sitting him in favor of José Caballero, who started in center field for the second time this season.
“Just felt like especially being on the turf here, he kind of jammed that heel in Minnesota and being on the turf [Friday], so I think it’s just a day-to-day kind of thing,” Boone said. “I even view him as available tonight.”
Boone said he preferred to keep Cody Bellinger in left field instead of shifting him to center.
“I considered moving him to center, but Belli’s grinding too and the turf here kind of beats you up,” he said. “There’s some scenarios where I would move him to center. Tonight, just being on the turf and as much as he’s been through this year, I didn’t want to move him.”
When the Yankees officially placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday, they opted for defensive versatility over offensive upside in his replacement.
That meant calling up Max Schuemann instead of Jasson Domínguez, giving the former another shot in the big leagues for at least a few days beginning this weekend against the Diamondbacks.
“Adding his versatility to our bench makes some sense,” Boone said. “And then obviously some different roster complications moving forward with the playoffs around the corner.”
Schuemann’s stay may be brief, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially returning from the IL as soon as the upcoming series against the Rays at Yankee Stadium that begins Tuesday.
If Schuemann goes back to Triple-A to make room, he would not be available to be recalled for 10 days (unless he was replacing an injured player again), essentially ruling him out as an option for the AL wild-card series.
That may have played a part in Domínguez not getting the call this time, in case the Yankees wanted to use him as a pinch-running threat on their playoff roster.
The 23-year-old also offers value as a switch-hitter, but he has proven to be a defensive liability in the outfield.
The Yankees’ trip to Chase Field gave them a chance to reunite with former teammate Jonathan Loáisiga, who has finally stayed healthy for a full season in the Diamondbacks bullpen.

The right-hander often flashed his talent during his eight-year tenure with the Yankees, but injuries too often got in the way.
This season, though, after signing a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks, Loáisiga has avoided the IL and pitched in a career-high 64 games with a 2.32 ERA entering Saturday.
“Been through a lot of battles over the years with Jonny,” Boone said. “It’ll be great to see him. Hopefully we can ding him a little bit here. I know he’s had a really strong year, which I’m excited about for him. He’s such a talented guy that for him, it’s always been about just being healthy. So the fact that he’s gone out there and had a largely healthy season, I’m not surprised at the success he’s had.”
The Diamondbacks held a 25th-anniversary celebration Saturday of their 2001 World Series team that beat the Yankees in seven games.

Last night was a good night for the Yankees, seeing the team put up five runs in the first paired with a good Gerrit Cole outing to cruise to a 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks. The club also picked up a game on the Rays as the AL East leaders dropped the opener of their series to the Red Sox. Tonight, the Yankees have two goals: get the win to stay in a hypothetically-competitive division race (all but necessary since Tampa Bay avenged the loss with a 2-1 win over Boston this afternoon), and build out a little more breathing room in the Cy Young race.
Dylan Cease had his worst start of the year on Friday for the Blue Jays, going just 2.2 innings and walking six. He and today's Yankee starter Cam Schlittler have had a heavyweight bout atop the Cy leaderboard all year, and while Cam's pulled away a bit in recent weeks, he can start to put the finishing touches on his case tonight. He hasn't allowed more than one earned run in a start since August 3rd (!!), making us all maybe expect a bit too much from the righty who can seemingly do no wrong. Schlittler has thrown 45 innings across those aforementioned seven starts, so he's not a five-and-fly guy, and his 1.00 ERA in that stretch is just…a farce.
Brandon Pfaadt is having the best season of his young career, with a 3.77 ERA and 4.06 FIP that are both significant steps forward after a pretty lost 2025. He doesn't strike many men out though, and a 45 percent ground ball rate means heavy sinking fastballs in the zone. There will be pitches to hit from Pfaadt; you just need to be able to elevate them.
Ben Rice had himself a fantastic game cleaning up last night and is bumped up to the leadoff spot tonight, with
Luis García Jr. getting the nod over Paul Goldschmidt at first base. Spencer Jones reportedly has a sore left foot, which means we get José Caballero in center, and I'm going to withhold comment on that decision for now.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees are already dealing with the loss of Aaron Judge, and now they have another outfielder on the MLB roster who is temporarily unavailable. Spencer Jones, one of New York’s biggest breakout stories over the past month, is out of Saturday’s lineup against the Arizona Diamondbacks with left foot soreness.
The rookie told MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch that he expects it to be a one-day issue, which should provide some relief for a Yankees team that cannot afford another significant injury.
Spencer Jones has become a key part of Yankees’ lineup
Jones’ emergence has been one of the more encouraging developments for New York this season. After struggling early in his rookie campaign, the 25-year-old has started to find his footing at the plate and has become the Yankees’ everyday center fielder.
Through his first 80 games, Jones is hitting .248/.318/.433 with 10 home runs and a 109 wRC+. More importantly, his September has been particularly impressive. He entered Saturday batting .340/.415/.532 with two homers, 12 RBIs and seven runs through his first 13 games of the month.
The Yankees have also been encouraged by the adjustments Jones has made against Major League pitching. Manager Aaron Boone previously compared his developmental path to Judge’s, noting that Jones’ enormous 6-foot-7 frame could become a major advantage as his adjustments continue to translate.
That makes Saturday’s lineup change particularly notable.
Yankees cannot afford another outfield injury
Jones is being held out as a precaution, with José Caballero taking over in center field Saturday. Jones has indicated that he expects to return Sunday, so there is currently no indication that the foot issue is expected to become a lengthy absence.
Still, the timing is less than ideal.
Judge officially returned to the injured list Saturday with a right calf strain and has no established timetable for his return. The Yankees recalled Max Schuemann to fill his roster spot, while the club is expected to rely more heavily on its remaining outfield options.
New York has already dealt with significant injuries across its roster this season. With the postseason approaching, the Yankees need Jones healthy and available because his recent production has given the lineup another legitimate offensive option.
For now, the hope is that Jones’ absence truly is nothing more than a one-day precaution.

The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

The New York Yankees are in the middle of a three-game series against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix.
New York won the first game of the series 9-2 on Friday. Game 2 is slated to begin at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday.
Before Saturday’s game, the Yankees announced a surprising lineup decision involving José Caballero.
New York Yankees Announce Interesting José Caballero Decision
Surprisingly, José Caballero will start in center field for the Yankees on Saturday. Caballero has played 11 innings in center this season and recorded 15 innings at the position last year.
Meanwhile, Spencer Jones, the Yankees’ primary center fielder, is out of the lineup with a sore left foot.
The New York Post’s Greg Joyce wrote on X: Spencer Jones said he’s dealing with a sore left foot, which he chalked up to the wear-and-tear from playing on turf. But downplayed it, said he’s fine, just getting a day. “It’s no big deal,” Jones said.
Here is the Yankees’ full lineup for Saturday:
- Ben Rice DH
- Cody Bellinger LF
- Luis Garcia Jr. 1B
- Heliot Ramos RF
- George Lombard Jr. SS
- Austin Wells C
- Anthony Volpe 2B
- Ryan McMahon 3B
- José Caballero CF
Starting Pitcher: RHP Cam Schlittler
Here is the Diamondbacks’ lineup:
- Laars Nootbar LF
- Ketel Marte 2B
- Gabriel Moreon C
- Geraldo Perdomo SS
- Corbin Carroll RF
- Nolan Arenado 3B
- Tim Tawa 1B

New York Yankees Right Now
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.
